newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Fighting said to mar Afghan truce for vaccinations.
newsitem.headline: Fighting said to mar Afghan truce for vaccinations.

text.p: New fighting erupted in the northwestern Afghan province of Badghis on Monday, breaking a U.N.-mediated five-day truce to help a polio vaccination campaign, a Pakistan-based Afghan news service reported.

The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted Taleban Islamic militia sources as saying fighting raged all day and the Taleban advanced at least eight km (five miles) in Bala Murghab area, after being attacked by northern Uzbek chief General Abdul Rashid Dostum's forces.

The U.N. children's fund UNICEF had earlier issued a statement in Islamabad saying the truce, negotiated by it and the World Health Organisation (WHO) and due to last from April 6-10, "is reported by UNICEF field offices to be holding throughout Afghanistan".
Dostum's jet fighters carried out heavy bombing of Taleban positions, AIP said, quoting a Taleban spokesman in the southern city of Kandahar.
There was no independent confirmation of the report, which said 16 of Dostum's and six Taleban troops were killed or wounded.
There was no immediate comment from the Taleban administration in the Afghan capital Kabul.
UNICEF said it launched the first of the planned two rounds of the polio immunisation campaign with the WHO and the Afghan Ministry of Public Health on Sunday.
It said it hoped that 3.8 million children under five years old would be given oral polio drops during the first round.
"Severe winter weather permitting, every district wil be covered for the first time," the statement said.
The vaccination campaign marks another step in a polio eradication initiative in the Middle East, the Caucasus and central Asia, UNICEF said.

The campaign was opened by Taleban Public Health Minister, Mullah Abbas Akhund, in Kabul and the head of political affairs in Dostum's administration, Nooruddin Hamsangar, in the northern city of Mazar-i-Sharif.
Afghanistan, devastated by more than 17 years of civil war, has had much of its health system destroyed.
UNICEF is supporting the campaign through the provision of polio vaccine, as well as equipment for the storage and transport of vaccines to vaccination posts, the statement said.
More than 13,000 health workers had been trained and mobilised for the operation.
The Dutch, Swedish and British governments as well as the European Community Humanitarian Office, the Centre for Disease Control in Atlanta and Rotary International have provided funds.
